value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: Response(siren_ringing, switch_toggled) treats the persistent siren_ringing condition as a new trigger on every step it remains true. That can leave a new switch_toggled promise pending after the siren is turned off, even though the task requires turning it off once each time it starts ringing. The clause needs to track ring starts, not every step of siren_ringing.

CHANGES REQUIRED: Response(served_while_ringing, switch_toggled) uses the wrong trigger. The task requires turning off the siren each time it starts ringing, but served_while_ringing only becomes true when an order is served during a ring. Use siren_ringing as the trigger for the required response to switch_toggled.

CHANGES REQUIRED: Response(siren_ringing, switch_toggled) is owed on every step the siren remains on, so toggling it off later does not satisfy the promise until the episode ends. The task says to turn it off each time it starts ringing; use Response on a start event, but no start event is declared. Add a proposition for the siren starting and bind the rule to that event.

CHANGES REQUIRED: Response(siren_ringing, switch_toggled) is too broad. The task says to turn the switch off each time the siren starts ringing, but this clause requires a toggle after every step the siren remains on and also permits the toggle on any later step. Use a rule that requires switch_toggled only when the siren starts ringing; the declared siren_ringing condition does not distinguish a start from continued ringing.

CHANGES REQUIRED: Response(siren_ringing, switch_toggled) applies whenever siren_ringing is true, not only when the siren starts. Because siren_ringing is a lasting condition, it becomes owed again on every ringing step; toggling the switch while the siren is on does not satisfy the promise until a later step, and the clause can remain pending at episode end. The task requires turning the siren off each time it starts, so use a rule tied to the start event rather than the lasting siren_ringing condition.

CHANGES REQUIRED: `Response(siren_ringing, switch_toggled)` does not capture “Each time the siren starts ringing”: `siren_ringing` is a lasting condition, so this rule is owed again on every step it remains true, and `switch_toggled` is a one-step event. Use `ChainResponse` from the ring-start event to `switch_toggled` if that event is represented; the declared `siren_ringing` condition does not identify when ringing starts.

CHANGES REQUIRED: Response(siren_ringing, switch_toggled) is owed on every step the siren remains on, so toggling it off later cannot satisfy the repeated obligations. The task says to turn it off each time it starts ringing. Use ChainResponse(siren_ringing, switch_toggled) to require the toggle on the very next step.
